title: REPORT on the implementation of the common security and defence policy – annual report 2024
part_text: 29. Underlines the need to further support the transition of development projects to marketable solutions and welcomes the provision in the EDIP proposal in that regard; deplores the unnecessary and dysfunctional duplication of efforts with regard to the hypersonic interceptor project, which does not meet the expectations of some Member States with more ambitious and advanced projects, and considers that the future main battle tank project does not meet the participation expectations of other Member States, thus increasing the risk that the final product will not meet the expectations of the countries concerned; notes that such actions counteract the ambition laid out in the EDIS to procure 60 % from the EDTIB by 2035, as scattered resources will extend the time required to achieve marketable solutions, thus most likely leading to procurement from the United States, which has modern, off-the-shelf, proven weapon systems; regrets, similarly, the mounting delays in essential capability projects, notably the Franco-German project on the Main Ground Combat System and the Franco-German-Spanish project on the Future Combat Air System, which also entail the risk of the future procurement of US solutions; stresses that all possible synergies with the EDF should be used, while avoiding the duplication of efforts;
